newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moroccan elections set for September - minister.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan elections set for September - minister.

text.p: Morocco will hold a general election in September and King Hassan will inaugurate the new parliament in October, visiting Moroccan Interior Minister Driss Basri said on Saturday.
Basri, in Paris to attend a meeting of interior ministers from the western Mediterranean, was commenting to reporters on democratic reforms to set up a bicameral parliamentary system.

He indicated that the constitutional reforms were partly intended to strengthen relations with Europe. "We want to anchor ourselves into Europe and we must present a liberal system respectful of liberties," he said.
He said radical Islamists would not be allowed to stand as their programme went against Morocco's tradition of tolerance.
"Admitting a totalitarian party with a religious basis would be the end of democracy in Morocco," he said.
Basri said moderate Islamists of the Reform and Renewal movement, which merged recently with the Constitutional Democratic and Popular Movement, would run but he expected them to fare poorly.
"They'll be happy if they win five seats," he said.
The opposition, led by the old-guard Istiqlal party and the Socialist Union of People's Forces, has 125 seats in the current 333-seat parliament.
The consitutional reforms, backed by the main opposition parties, were passed in a 1996 referendum.

The government and the 12 political parties represented in the current 333-seat parliament signed last February an agreement to help ensure that the planned elections in 25,000 communal and municipal centres, including the disputed Western Sahara, be fair and honest.
